item.title: Thu PM · Philosophize This!: Episode #047 ... Rousseau pt. 3 - The General Will
item.itunes:title: Thu PM · Philosophize This!: Episode #047 ... Rousseau pt. 3 - The General Will
item.description:
On this episode of the podcast, we continue our desert island thought experiment, this time focusing on the general will of the people. First, we examine several interpretations of what "the general will of the people" actually means. Next, we take an in-depth look at Rousseau's interpretation, and discuss the difference between democratic and transcendental will. Finally, we explore the multitude of complications that arise when a government tries to enact the general will after it's (somewhat) agreed upon. All this and more on the latest episode of Philosophize This!

item.title: Thu AM · Wildcard · In Our Time: Immune cells
item.itunes:title: Thu AM · Wildcard · In Our Time: Immune cells
item.description:
Every day, billions of specialised cells work to protect your body from harm. From the common cold and infections to cuts and scrapes or cancerous cells, our bodies deal with a range of potential threats and risks as we move through the world. The immune system is a complex and carefully orchestrated network connecting organs, tissues, and billions of specialised cells. Those cells have a variety of different roles as they respond to pathogens or harm, including engulfing microbes, identifying damage, or producing antibodies. Misha Glenny and his guests examine the different types of cells involved in an immune response, how they know what to respond to, and what happens when those cells aren’t working as they should. This In Our Time episode discusses why our immune cells are vital to life – both for us as individuals, and as a species. The discussion explores the interconnected nature of the immune system, and what we know actually affects the way our immune cells function. item.title: Thu AM · The Mortise & Tenon Podcast: 40 – Defining “Craftsmanship”
item.itunes:title: Thu AM · The Mortise & Tenon Podcast: 40 – Defining “Craftsmanship”
item.description:
In this latest podcast episode, Joshua and Mike tackle a particularly thorny question head on: What is “craftsmanship,” exactly? While woodworkers of all kinds share a mutual appreciation for craftsmanship, surprisingly, there have been different ideas of what it even means. Is “craftsmanship” the same thing as “making” or is there something more to it? Can woodworking skill be reduced to the ability to repeat precise hand motions? Joshua and Mike argue that there’s more to it than that.

Throughout the course of the discussion, they explain that the aim of technology is to displace skill for the sake of ease and precision. While technical developments provide real, tangible blessings in so many areas of life, Joshua and Mike contend that it is worth pondering how the “technologizing” of our craft can diminish its splendor.

From The Mortise & Tenon Podcast, first released February 24, 2022.

item.title: Wed PM · Wildcard · Hit Parade: With or Without U2 Edition Part 1
item.itunes:title: Wed PM · Wildcard · Hit Parade: With or Without U2 Edition Part 1
item.description:
U2 have millions of admirers—and haters: from the fans who regard them as rock’s conscience, to the cynics who blanch at lead singer Bono’s self-importance. Here’s the thing: U2 want to play to both crowds. They know why the haters can’t stand them. After a decade of earnestness in the ’80s, Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen called BS on themselves, rebooting their sound and image for the ’90s age of irony.

This shouldn’t have worked. Instead, U2 became as big as ever, and kept scoring hits. Then, when the whole sardonic thing stopped working for them, at the turn of the millennium, they went back to anthemic U2—and the hits kept coming. Their ability to pivot so many times and keep scoring hits over multiple decades is rare in pop history.

Join Chris Molanphy as he explains how U2 pulled this off. How did they balance cool and cringe? How did they outlast new wave, college rock, hair metal and grunge to remain chart-toppers into the era of teenpop and hip-hop? And…what exactly were they thinking when they forced an album onto your iPhone? They don’t mean to bug ya, but…why can’t we live with or without U2?

Podcast production by Kevin Bendis.

﻿Disclosure in Podc

From Hit Parade, first released October 11, 2024.

item.title: Wed PM · ShopNotes Podcast: ShopNotes Podcast E293: Personality: ACTIVATED
item.itunes:title: Wed PM · ShopNotes Podcast: ShopNotes Podcast E293: Personality: ACTIVATED
item.description:
What's the secret to finding great vintage woodworking tools at antique stores? In ShopNotes Podcast Episode 293, Phil Huber, Logan Wittmer, and John Doyle talk about hunting for old hand tools, spotting hidden treasures, and knowing when you've found a good deal.

Phil shares his latest antique mall finds, including vintage T-handle augers and a six-foot Lufkin wooden ruler. Logan explains his methodical approach to searching antique stores, what he looks for in vintage hand planes, and why some of the best woodworking tools aren't always found in the display cases.

Along the way, the guys discuss identifying valuable tools, negotiating prices, finding unusual materials for woodworking projects, and collecting furniture design inspiration.

But first, there's some unfinished business from last week's episode: Logan finally explains why he stopped wearing Crocs in the shop! That leads to a lively discussion about shop footwear, comfortable work boots, and how long shoes really last in a woodworking shop.

In this episode: • Logan's great shop shoe debate: Crocs, Hey Dudes, and work boots • Finding vintage woodworking tools at antique malls • Tips for spotting bargains on old hand

From ShopNotes Podcast, first released November 20, 2026.

item.itunes:title: Tue AM · PsycHacks: Episode 677: Don't take her out (the principle of anti-dating)
item.description:
Don’t take her out if you’re looking for a long-term relationship. Instead, court her in the context of the life you already lead. In this episode, I introduce the principle of anti-dating, arguing that conventional dates either provide irrelevant information or create a misleading idea of what an eventual relationship will look like. Inviting a potential partner into your everyday routine will reveal far more useful data than expensive dinners, elaborate activities, or structured interviews ever could.

item.itunes:title: Tue AM · Wildcard · Overdue: Ep 328 - The Indian In The Cupboard, by Lynne Reid Banks
item.description:
When we talk about judging books by the standards of their time, we’re usually dealing with books that have been written many many decades ago, but Lynne Reid Banks’ The Indian In The Cupboard isn’t far removed from our own childhoods. It’s easy to see why the book resonates with kids, but it’s also frustrating to see Banks acknowledging the gap between pop culture depictions and reality even as she feeds into so many stereotypes. item.itunes:title: Mon PM · 60 Songs That Explain the '90s: Shakira — “Hips Don’t Lie”
item.description:
This episode is for the ladies up in here tonight! Before her hips became internationally renowned, Shakira was making Spanish rock music from the age of 14. Today, Rob looks back at her crossover album 'Laundry Service,' which was released as other Latin American artists were also starting to make music in English. Later, he is joined by music journalist Suzy Exposito, who talks about why Shakira deserves to be in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, her initial disappointment when Shakira dyed her hair blonde and started singing in English, and what it was like getting to interview her.

item.description:
We are sharing an episode from one of the brilliant podcasts on the RQ Network, The 100 Handed.

The 100 Handed is a Paranormal Urban Fantasy Podcast.

Weep at the wonder. Howl at the horror. The tattooed magician Evan Wexler and his werewolf partner V spend their nights prowling a shadowy Texas underbelly full of frenzied monsters and mad sorcerers. Working for the mysterious organization known only as the Madhouse, they struggle to contain the threat of the Gloom, a malevolent force that breathes life into humanity’s worst nightmares and can make a heart’s darkest desires come true. This is The 100 Handed. The 100 Handed is an urban fantasy-horror audio drama set in Texas, drawing inspiration from the works of Clive Barker and Tim Powers as well as shows such as Bleach and Fate. This fiction podcast chronicles the budding shadow war between two groups of magicians, with disastrous consequences. The content is frequently explicit and intended for mature audiences only. Consider yourself warned.
